question: Why is document text exposed through a function tool rather than injected directly into the LLM context with every message?
options: LiveKit data channels cannot carry text content directly to the LLM
The LLM cannot read text longer than 1,000 tokens in a single context
Function tools are faster than context injection for text processing
It keeps token usage under control by letting the LLM retrieve document content only when it needs to reference it
explanation: A long document could contain thousands of tokens. Injecting it into every LLM call would waste tokens on turns where the document is not relevant. The function tool pattern lets the LLM decide when to retrieve the content, keeping costs proportional to actual usage.

question: Why do screen share captures use a higher max_width (1920) compared to camera captures (1024)?
options: Screen shares are always displayed on larger monitors
The browser's getDisplayMedia API requires a minimum resolution of 1920 pixels
Screen content contains small text that becomes unreadable if downscaled too aggressively
Higher resolution reduces the token cost per frame for screen content
explanation: Screen content is primarily text and UI elements rendered at specific font sizes. Downscaling to 1024px can make small text unreadable to the LLM. The tradeoff is higher token cost (1500-2000 tokens per frame), but accuracy on screen content is worth it.

question: Why does the annotation system use normalized coordinates (0-1) instead of pixel coordinates?
options: LLMs can only output floating-point numbers between 0 and 1
Normalized coordinates decouple the annotation from screen resolution, working correctly on both 1080p and 4K displays
The HTML canvas element only accepts percentage-based positioning
Pixel coordinates would exceed the maximum data message payload size
explanation: Normalized coordinates are resolution-independent. The frontend maps them to actual pixel positions based on the current display size. This means the same annotation coordinates work correctly whether the user is on a 1080p laptop or a 4K monitor.
